title: Rigid Embedding of Fixed and Stained, Whole, Millimeter-Scale Specimens for Section-free 3D Histology by Micro-Computed Tomography
protocol: Starve juvenile fish for at least 24 hours for a 10 mm specimen, or longer for larger specimens (e.g., 72 hours for a 14 mm specimen).
Pre-chill 10% Neutral Buffered Formalin and 2x Tricaine-S on ice to 4°C.
Double the fish water volume with chilled 2x MS-222 for rapid euthanasia.
Wait for 30 seconds (larvae) to 60 seconds (juveniles) after the fish stops moving.
Immerse the fish in chilled 10% NBF for 10 minutes.
Fix the fish in chilled 10% NBF solution overnight in flat-bottomed containers at room temperature.
For larger fish, slit the belly starting slightly anterior to the anal pore using minimal penetration and gentle force away from the fish.
Rinse fixed specimens three times in 1x phosphate buffered saline (PBS) pH 7.4 for 10 min.
Submerge samples in 35% ethyl alcohol (EtOH) for 20 min at room temperature with gentle agitation.
Submerge samples in 50% EtOH for 20 min at room temperature with gentle agitation.
Dissolve phosphotungstic acid (PTA) powder in water to prepare a 1% w/v stock solution.
Dilute the 1% PTA stock solution 3:7 in 100% EtOH to obtain a 0.3% PTA staining solution.
Stain samples overnight in the 0.3% PTA solution at room temperature with gentle agitation.
Prepare a 1:1 v/v mixture of 100% EtOH and LR White acrylic resin.
Rinse samples three times in 70% EtOH for 10 min.
Submerge samples in 90% EtOH for 30 min at room temperature with gentle agitation.
Submerge samples in 95% EtOH for 30 min at room temperature with gentle agitation.
Submerge samples twice in 100% EtOH for 30 min at room temperature with gentle agitation.
Submerge samples in the 1:1 EtOH and LR White acrylic resin mixture overnight at room temperature with gentle agitation.
Submerge samples in 100% LR White resin for 2 h at room temperature with gentle agitation.
Replace the resin in step 4.1 with fresh 100% LR White resin.
Incubate for 1 hour at room temperature with gentle agitation.
Cut polyimide tubing to an appropriate diameter and length.
Attach a P1000 micropipette to the wide end of the embedding adapter.
Insert the polyimide tubing to the narrow end of the embedding adapter.
Clip off the end of a micropipette tip straight across such that it fits snugly with the polyimide tubing.
Cut 44 mm from the wide end of a 200 µL yellow micropipette tip for 0.0403" tubing.
Cut 59 mm from the bottom of a 1 mL blue tip for 0.105" tubing.
Trim as needed to fit the polyimide tubing.
Attach the cut micropipette tip to a micropipette.
Transfer samples to a small weigh boat or V-shaped solution basin.
Fully submerge the samples in 100% LR White resin.
Aim the tubing at the wide end of the fixed sample or towards the head for animal specimens.
Pipette the specimen slowly into the tubing using the micropipette.
Position the sample in the middle of the tubing.
Ensure that the tubing above and below the specimen is filled with resin.
Pipette the sample into the tubing such that the sample is moving in the natural, forward direction.
Flatten the oil-based soft modeling clay into a 1 mm-thick sheet.
Stabilize the tubing between index and middle fingers.
Slowly press the clay against the end of the tubing with thumb.
Remove excess clay.
Remove the embedding apparatus from the micropipette.
Pull out the tubing by gentle rotation and seal the other end with the clay.
Hold a finger against the sealed end to prevent the ejection of the clay.
Slowly push the unsealed end of the tubing into the clay.
Place the tubing horizontally.
Polymerize the resin for 24 h at 65 °C.
Collect samples for image acquisition at the end of Day 5.
Determine an optimal X-ray energy range of 5-30 keV for imaging PTA-stained zebrafish.
Use an X-ray energy of 13.8 keV for micro-CT imaging.
Obtain 1501 projections over 180 degrees at 13.8 keV, with a projection every 0.12 degrees.
Acquire two flat-field (gain) images and one dark-field image during the acquisition process.
Perform flat-field and dark-field corrections on the acquired images.
Reduce ring artifacts in the images.
Reconstruct the images using TomoPy toolkit.
Scan PTA-stained Daphnia and Drosophila samples on an X-ray microscope.
Set micro-CT parameters such as 40 kVp, 74 mA, and 15 s for Drosophila imaging at a voxel resolution of 3.10 × 3.10 × 3.10 µm³.
